root_cause.text: Holding the per-VMA lock (vma->vm_lock) across the BPF program body in the task_vma iterator creates a lock ordering deadlock (vm_lock → i_rwsem → mmap_lock → vm_lock) when BPF helpers acquire locks that depend on mmap_lock.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states "Holding the per-VMA lock across the BPF program body creates a lock ordering problem when helpers acquire locks that depend on mmap_lock: vm_lock -> i_rwsem -> mmap_lock -> vm_lock". The patch replaces the `locked_vma` pointer (which kept the lock held) with a `snapshot` of the VMA obtained via `memcpy` under the lock, then drops the lock (`vma_end_read(vma)`) before returning the snapshot to the BPF program, preventing the lock from being held during program execution.
